::: {#rem-tm-robustness-proof}
#### Simulations behind @thm-tm-robustness

@arora2009computational [section 1.3] prove all three parts by simulation.
For part 1, the new machine writes each symbol of $M$'s alphabet
as a block of about $\log_2 s$ binary digits,
and it carries out one step of $M$ by reading and rewriting one block on each tape.
For part 2, the single tape holds the contents of all $k$ tapes interleaved,
with a mark at each head's position.
To carry out one step of $M$,
the machine sweeps along the used part of the tape to read the marked symbols,
and sweeps back to update them.
After $t$ steps, $M$ has used at most $\max(n, t) + 1$ cells of each tape,
which is $\asymub{T(n)}$ because $T(n) \ge n$,
so each sweep takes $\asymub{T(n)}$ steps,
and the $T(n)$ steps of $M$ take $\asymub{T(n)^2}$ in all.
For part 3, the new machine first copies the input onto a work tape,
which stands in for $M$'s input tape.
It folds each of $M$'s tapes in half at the cell holding $\triangleright$,
so that cell $i$ of a folded tape holds the pair of symbols
$i$ cells to the right and $i$ cells to the left of $\triangleright$.
It remembers in its state which half each head is in,
so it carries out each step of $M$ in a constant number of steps.
At the end it unfolds $M$'s output onto its own output tape.
The input has $n$ symbols,
which is at most $T(n)$,
and the output has at most $T(n)$ symbols,
so the copy and the unfolding take $\asymub{T(n)}$ steps each.

:::
